_comment: Lite Cookbook — a small curated table of CPU-friendly quantized models, tiered by total system RAM. NOT the 270-model upstream scanner. Sizes/speeds are realistic CPU-only estimates; tokens_per_sec is a rough range on a modern dual/quad-core with no GPU. Keep this list short and honest.

tiers.label: 2–4 GB RAM
tiers.summary: Very low RAM. Expect short answers and slow generation. Best for simple Q&A, drafting, and tool-calling — not long reasoning.

models.name: llama3.2:1b
models.note: Smallest viable instruct model; fast, limited reasoning.

models.name: qwen2.5:0.5b
models.note: Tiny; good for classification/extraction, weak at open chat.

models.name: gemma2:2b
models.note: Borderline on 4GB; close other apps first.

tiers.label: 4–8 GB RAM
tiers.summary: The sweet spot for lite. 3B-class instruct models give usable chat, summarization, and agent tool use at tolerable speed.

models.name: llama3.2:3b
models.note: Recommended default — good balance of quality and speed.

models.name: qwen2.5:3b
models.note: Strong at structured output and tool calls.

tiers.label: 8 GB+ RAM
tiers.summary: Room for 7B-class models. Noticeably better reasoning and longer context, still CPU-only but slower per token.

models.name: llama3.1:8b
models.note: Best general quality in the lite range; needs ~8GB free.

api_fallback.summary: No local model is comfortable on this machine — or you just want the best quality. Use a hosted API instead. Set the provider key in Settings or .env and pick a small, cheap model.
